research.job_description_summary: Qualcomm hires engineers in India (Hyderabad, Bengaluru) for software, embedded and validation roles. A May 2026 Glassdoor review describes an online assessment (aptitude 20, maths 20, programming 20), a first technical round on OS and DSA (process versus thread), a second technical round on low-level C/C++, OOP, a HackerRank DSA problem and a bit-flip question, and an HR round. A 2026 hiring post lists C, OS and DSA. The official careers page was not fetched.
limitations: Qualcomm's official careers page was not fetched, so no round is marked DOCUMENTED.

Candidate-attributed material is essentially one Glassdoor review (May 2026; exact day not captured, recorded as the 1st of the month); only process versus thread and the bit-flip question are reported as questions, so only 2 items carry class B and are unverified.
The freshershunt hiring post is undated in the capture (recorded as 2026-01-01 as a placeholder) and gives topics only.
An older LeetCode Discuss post and 2015/2024 Jointaro experiences were seen but are outside the recency window and used only as context.
The Validation Engineer track is inferred from the review's mention of validation, VLSI, digital electronics and C topics; its content is original practice.
Aptitude and maths items are original practice; section sizes come from the single review.

Evidence handling: practice questions cite no sources; where a source only supplied topic context it is named in the question notes. Practice and job-description-inferred questions are UNVERIFIED and capped at LOW confidence on import.

Review status: answers, samples and cited counts come from the researcher and were not independently re-run; spot checks only. Source titles and some dates are blank because the sources did not show them.
Source pages on LeetCode Discuss and Glassdoor returned HTTP 403 to the CodeArena audit tool (2026-10-11), so the cited questions were not re-confirmed against those pages.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a process and a thread?
questions.relevance_to_role: A May 2026 Glassdoor review describes a first technical round on OS (process versus thread) and data structures; a 2026 hiring post lists C, OS and DSA.
questions.expected_answer: A process has its own address space and resources; threads in a process share code, heap and files but have their own stack and registers. Thread switches are cheaper; processes isolate faults.
follow_ups: What does a thread not share?
questions.notes: Candidate-reported question (May 2026 review), paraphrased; not verified.

questions.prompt: What happens during a context switch and why is it costly?
questions.relevance_to_role: A May 2026 Glassdoor review describes a first technical round on OS (process versus thread) and data structures; a 2026 hiring post lists C, OS and DSA.
questions.expected_answer: The kernel saves the registers and program counter of the running task into its PCB and loads another's; caches and TLB lose locality, so performance dips.
follow_ups: How do threads reduce the cost?
questions.notes: The source lists topics, not reported questions. Topic context only (no candidate attribution): https://www.glassdoor.co.in/Interview/Qualcomm-Interview-E640-RVW81941403.htm.

questions.expected_answer: A mutex gives exclusive ownership of a critical section; a counting semaphore controls access to N resources or signals between threads.

questions.prompt: What is virtual memory and what is a page fault?
questions.relevance_to_role: A May 2026 Glassdoor review describes a first technical round on OS (process versus thread) and data structures; a 2026 hiring post lists C, OS and DSA.
questions.expected_answer: Each process sees a private address space mapped to physical frames via page tables; a page fault occurs when the page is not resident and the OS must load it.
follow_ups: What is thrashing?
